description: One Feature: its Traces, blockers first, each on its own branch of the stack. Then the checkpoint: the validator verifies and tunes, the night waits for CI, the orchestrator steers, and a rule continues or halts the night.

inputs.name: item
inputs.label: The Feature
inputs.description: The Feature issue, one element of the night's list of sub-issues of the Epic.

outputs.name: prs
outputs.description: The pull requests of the Traces, bottom to top.

outputs.name: tune_pr
outputs.description: The tuning pull request, or empty.

outputs.name: ci
outputs.description: done when CI was green, timeout when it was not in time.

nodes.label: Start of the Feature
nodes.command:
# Where this Feature starts, for the checkpoint after its Traces.
set -e
mkdir -p .build/night
git branch --show-current > .build/night/feature-start-branch
git rev-parse HEAD > .build/night/feature-base
gh issue view "{{item.number}}" --json body --jq .body > .build/night/FEATURE.md

nodes.label: Every Trace built?
nodes.prompt: The checkpoint runs only when every Trace of the Feature has its pull request. Else the Feature fails, and the Features that wait on it are blocked.

options.name: nothing
options.description: No Trace was left to build.
options.when: traces.done_count = 0 and traces.failed_count = 0 and traces.blocked_count = 0 and traces.waiting_count = 0

options.name: incomplete
options.description: A Trace failed, is blocked, or still waits.

options.name: complete
options.description: Every Trace is built: run the checkpoint.

nodes.label: No checkpoint
nodes.command:
# Not every Trace is built: say so on the Feature, go back to where the Feature started, and fail. The Features that wait on this one are blocked.
counts=$(printf 'Built: %s, failed: %s, blocked: %s, waiting: %s.' "{{traces.done_count}}" "{{traces.failed_count}}" "{{traces.blocked_count}}" "{{traces.waiting_count}}")
printf 'Not every Trace of Feature #%s is built, so the checkpoint did not run.\n\n%s\n\n%s\n' "{{item.number}}" "$counts" "{{traces.summary}}"
printf '### night-shift: the build stopped before the checkpoint\n\n%s\n\n%s\n' "$counts" "{{traces.summary}}" | gh issue comment "{{item.number}}" --body-file - || true
# The next Feature must not build on the work of a failed Trace. That work stays on its own branch, committed.
start=$(cat .build/night/feature-start-branch)
if [ "$(git branch --show-current)" != "$start" ] && [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
	git add -A
	git commit --no-verify -qm "wip: the build of Feature #{{item.number}} that stopped" || true
fi
git checkout -q "$start" || true
exit 1

nodes.label: tune/ branch
nodes.command:
# A tune/ branch on top of the stack, and the context of the check for the whole Feature.
set -e
git branch --show-current > .build/night/tune-base-branch
git rev-parse HEAD > .build/night/tune-base
git checkout --no-track -B "tune/{{item.number}}"
rm -f .build/night/REPORT.md
printf '%s' "{{scenarios.data.scenarios}}" > .build/night/feature-scenarios.json
python3 -c '
import json
names = json.load(open(".build/night/feature-scenarios.json"))
base = open(".build/night/feature-base").read().strip()
json.dump({"base": base, "sim": "rpg-pool-1", "scenarios": names}, open(".build/night/context.json", "w"))
print(len(names), "claimed scenario(s) in this Feature.")
'

nodes.label: Validator

summary.description: 3 to 6 sentences: how good the build was, and what you changed.

note.description: What is wrong or weak, when something is.

needs_owner.description: Each step or decision that only the owner can take.

nodes.prompt:
You are the validator at the checkpoint of an unattended night build ("night-shift"). The worker built all Traces of Feature #{{item.number}} ({{item.title}}). Each Trace has its pull request on the stack. After you, the orchestrator reads your findings, steers the next work, and a rule decides whether the night continues. Nobody is awake. Do not ask a question: decide, act, and write down what you decided.

You are in the worktree, on a `tune/` branch on top of the stack. It gets a pull request of its own when it has a commit. The work to validate is `git diff "$(cat .build/night/feature-base)..HEAD"`. The Traces of this Feature, as the build left them:
{{traces.summary}}
The scenarios they claim: {{scenarios.data.scenarios}}
The issues: `gh issue view <number>`. `.build/night/FEATURE.md` holds the Feature.

Do these two tasks, in this order.

1. VERIFY. A claimed scenario is verified when a test with its exact name exists, passes, and asserts each Then step for real. Look at each Trace. Look at the tests that existed before (`git diff "$(cat .build/night/feature-base)..HEAD" -- Packages/Tests`): a worker that weakened or removed an assert to get a green check is the worst case. Check the rules below, the contracts of each Trace, and the Golden fixtures that changed.

2. TUNE. Correct what is wrong or weak, here, on this branch: a deviation from the spec, an assert that is missing, a broken rule, dead code, a wrong domain term, a seam that the next Features cannot build on. A bug gets a failing test first, then the fix, in its own `fix(...)` commit. Small Conventional Commits. Do not rewrite what is good: the goal is a correct and clean base for the next work, not your taste. No change is a good result when the work is good.
   Do not change the scenario set. Do not edit an issue. Do not push, open a pull request, or merge: a later step does the delivery and the labels.
   After a change, run `python3 tools/night-shift/night-shift.py gate` until it prints `GATE PASSED`. It can take 20 minutes: give your shell tool the timeout 2700000 (milliseconds) for it.

Then report. The data of your step report holds `summary` (3 to 6 sentences: how good the build was, and what you changed), `traces` (one entry per Trace: its `number`, `verified`, and a `note` when something is wrong or weak) and `needs_owner` (each step or decision for the owner). When the code misses its spec in a way that you could not correct here, or the spec contradicts itself or the code, say so in the summary and in the note of the Trace: the orchestrator decides what happens next.

When this message comes again in the same session, your tuning did not pass the check after you. Its result (empty the first time):

```
{{check_tune.log_tail}}
```

Then correct the cause, commit, run the check until it prints `GATE PASSED`, and report again. When the check still fails after this, a later step removes your changes; your findings still count.

Rules of this repository:

- Tests: Swift Testing. Each claimed scenario gets one test with the scenario name as the exact `@Test("...")` display name. Test logic, not pixels: tests of pure package code, and `Edge/` tests that drive the store, the scene, or the view model. No new XCUITest. The UI smoke set (`App/UITests/SmokeUITests.swift`) must keep passing.
- The model is a fake in each test (see the test doubles of ModelRuntime). No test asks a real model.
- Determinism: each random number comes from a Seed Stream (`SeedStream`). No `random()`, no `Date()`, and no frame time in the simulation. The simulation has 30 Ticks each second. A test steps Ticks with recorded inputs; it does not sleep and does not use real time.
- Game State is `Codable`. Each new Game State field goes into the save round-trip test of the Run File.
- Golden fixtures (`Packages/Tests/Fixtures/`): change one only when the Trace changes the rules on purpose. Record it again with `TEST_RUNNER_RECORD_GOLDEN_SEEDS=1`, read the diff, and commit the fixture in its own commit with the reason.
- Verticals: pure code imports no SwiftUI, SpriteKit, UIKit, or DesignSystem outside an `Edge/` folder. A new target needs its target and its test target in `Packages/Package.swift`, and its entry in `tools/ci/verticals.json`, in the same commit.
- Wide Events: one event for each unit of work, emitted one time in a `defer`. No `print`. No text of the Player and no text of the model in an event.
- The build has no warnings (a warning is an error). `swift format lint --strict --recursive App Packages` passes.
- Code and comments describe the code as it is now: no history, no old names, no issue numbers, no milestone names.
- Names use the domain terms of `docs/glossary.md`. A generic mechanism gets a generic name.
- A bug in existing code: first a test that fails, then the fix, in its own `fix(...)` commit.
- Commits: small Conventional Commits (`feat(run): ...`, `test(direction): ...`) in simple English, with the trailer lines `Scenario: <scenario name>` and `Trace: #<number>`.
- Do not change `.github/`, the scripts and the allow lists of `tools/ci/`, signing, entitlements, or the settings of the Apple developer account. Do not delete or weaken a test to make it pass.
- `xcodebuild test` gets `-collect-test-diagnostics never -parallel-testing-enabled NO`. A Swift Testing `-only-testing` ID of one test needs `()` at its end. Use only the Simulator `rpg-pool-1`; do not make or delete a Simulator. Logs go into `.build/logs/`.
- These rules are the short form of `docs/steering/` (TECH.md, QA.md). Read a section there only when a rule above does not answer your question.

nodes.label: Check the tuning
nodes.command:
# The check after the validator: no loose changes, then the script's own gate over the whole Feature.
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
	echo '`git status` shows changes that are not committed:'
	git status --porcelain | head -25
	exit 1
fi
python3 tools/night-shift/night-shift.py gate

nodes.label: Remove the tuning
nodes.command:
# The tuning did not pass the check: remove it. The findings of the validator still count.
git reset -q --hard "$(cat .build/night/tune-base)"
git clean -qfd
echo "The changes of the validator did not pass the check. They are removed."

nodes.label: Tuning PR, labels, comment
nodes.command:
# The tune/ branch gets a pull request on the stack when it has a commit. Then the label `verified` per Trace and a comment on the Feature, from the validator's report. Prints the tuning pull request as JSON.
set -e
# Everything below goes to the log. Only the JSON at the end is the output.
exec 3>&1 1>&2
branch="tune/{{item.number}}"
base_branch=$(cat .build/night/tune-base-branch)
url=""
if [ "$(git rev-list --count "$(cat .build/night/tune-base)..HEAD")" != 0 ]; then
	git push --force-with-lease -u origin "$branch"
	# A base branch that is not on GitHub (the run's own branch): the pull request goes on the trunk.
	git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "$base_branch" >/dev/null || base_branch=$(gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name)
	{
		printf '## Summary\n\nThe tuning of Feature #%s (%s) after its build: the validator at the checkpoint of the night build.\n\n%s\n' "{{item.number}}" "{{item.title}}" "{{validate.data.summary}}"
		printf '\n## Changes\n\n'
		git log --reverse --format='- %s' "$(cat .build/night/tune-base)..HEAD"
		printf '\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] The local check against the start of the Feature: the guards, the format lint, the tests of the affected Verticals, and, for a change in `App/` or `Edge/`, the app builds and the UI smoke set\n\n## Related\n\nFeature #%s\n' "{{item.number}}"
	} > .build/night/pr-body.md
	url=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty')
	if [ -z "$url" ]; then
		url=$(gh pr create --base "$base_branch" --head "$branch" --title "refactor: tune {{item.title}}" --body-file .build/night/pr-body.md)
		url=$(printf '%s\n' "$url" | tail -1)
	fi
	[ -n "$url" ] || { echo "No tuning pull request was opened."; exit 1; }
	echo "Tuning: $url"
else
	git checkout -q "$base_branch"
	git branch -q -D "$branch"
	echo "The validator changed nothing: no tuning pull request."
fi
# The labels and the comment, from the validator's report (empty when it gave none).
python3 -c '
import json, subprocess, sys
feature, url = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[3]
report = json.loads(sys.argv[2] or "{}")
lines = ["### night-shift: checkpoint after the build", "", str(report.get("summary") or "The validator gave no report.")]
for result in report.get("traces") or []:
    number, verified = str(result.get("number", "")), bool(result.get("verified"))
    if verified and number.isdigit():
        subprocess.run(["gh", "issue", "edit", number, "--add-label", "verified"], check=False)
    note = (". " + str(result["note"])) if result.get("note") else ""
    lines.append("- Trace #" + number + ": " + ("verified" if verified else "NOT verified") + note)
needs = report.get("needs_owner") or []
if needs:
    lines += ["", "Needs the owner:"] + ["- " + str(item) for item in needs]
if url:
    lines += ["", "Tuning: " + url]
subprocess.run(["gh", "issue", "comment", feature, "--body-file", "-"], input="\n".join(lines) + "\n", text=True, check=True)
' "{{item.number}}" "{{validate.data}}" "$url"
# The commit that the orchestrator must leave as it is.
git rev-parse HEAD > .build/night/tuned
printf '{"url": "%s"}\n' "$url" >&3

until.command:
# Exit 0 when every pull request of the Feature, the tuning one too, has green checks or no checks. Else the wait sleeps and tries again.
# A red check also tries again: the wait cannot end early as failed, so it ends at its time limit.
{
	printf '%s' "{{prs.data.urls}}" | python3 -c 'import json, sys; print("\n".join(json.load(sys.stdin)))'
	printf '%s\n' "{{deliver_tune.data.url}}"
} | while read -r url; do
	[ -n "$url" ] || continue
	checks=$(gh pr checks "$url" 2>&1) && continue
	case "$checks" in
	*"no checks reported"*) continue ;;
	esac
	printf '%s is not green yet:\n%s\n' "$url" "$checks"
	exit 1
done

nodes.label: Orchestrator: steer

sound_base.description: true when the next Features can build on this code. false when work on top of it would be wrong: the code misses its spec in a way the validator could not correct, or the spec contradicts itself or the code.

report.description: 3 to 6 sentences: how good the work of this Feature is, and why the base is sound or not.

needs_owner.description: Each step or decision for the owner.

nodes.prompt:

{{validate.data.summary}}

Its verdict per Trace: {{validate.data.traces}}
The tuning of the validator, when it did not pass the check, was removed ("pass" here means removed, empty means kept): {{drop_tune.outcome}}
CI on the pull requests of this Feature: {{ci.outcome}} after {{ci.waited_minutes}} minutes ("timeout" means CI was not green in time: look at `gh pr checks <url>` for {{prs.data.urls}} and say in your report what is red).

{{traces.summary}}
The issues: `gh issue view <number>`. `.build/night/FEATURE.md` holds the Feature.
Do not change the code and do not commit: you steer the next work. A rule after you reads your report and decides whether the night continues.

- `.build/night/steering/trace-<number>.md`: a note for one of those Traces, only when you have a concrete fact for it (for example "the type that the Trace calls X is `Y` in `File.swift`").

Then report. The data of your step report holds `sound_base`, `report` and `needs_owner`. Set `sound_base` to false only when work on top of this code would be wrong: the code misses its spec in a way that the validator could not correct, or the spec contradicts itself or the code so that the owner must decide. In each other case it is true. In `report`: 3 to 6 sentences on how good the work of this Feature is and why the base is sound or not. In `needs_owner`: each step or decision for the owner.

Rules of this repository:

- Verticals: pure code imports no SwiftUI, SpriteKit, UIKit, or DesignSystem outside an `Edge/` folder. A new target needs its target and its test target in `Packages/Package.swift`, and its entry in `tools/ci/verticals.json`, in the same commit.
- Wide Events: one event for each unit of work, emitted one time in a `defer`. No `print`. No text of the Player and no text of the model in an event.
- The build has no warnings (a warning is an error). `swift format lint --strict --recursive App Packages` passes.
- Code and comments describe the code as it is now: no history, no old names, no issue numbers, no milestone names.
- Names use the domain terms of `docs/glossary.md`. A generic mechanism gets a generic name.
- A bug in existing code: first a test that fails, then the fix, in its own `fix(...)` commit.
- Commits: small Conventional Commits (`feat(run): ...`, `test(direction): ...`) in simple English, with the trailer lines `Scenario: <scenario name>` and `Trace: #<number>`.
- Do not change `.github/`, the scripts and the allow lists of `tools/ci/`, signing, entitlements, or the settings of the Apple developer account. Do not delete or weaken a test to make it pass.
- `xcodebuild test` gets `-collect-test-diagnostics never -parallel-testing-enabled NO`. A Swift Testing `-only-testing` ID of one test needs `()` at its end. Use only the Simulator `rpg-pool-1`; do not make or delete a Simulator. Logs go into `.build/logs/`.

nodes.label: Keep the code as tuned
nodes.command:
# The orchestrator must not change the code: remove a change of it. Its notes in .build/night/ stay (git ignores that folder).
tuned=$(cat .build/night/tuned)
if [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" != "$tuned" ] || [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
	git reset -q --hard "$tuned"
	git clean -qfd
	echo "The orchestrator changed the code, and it must not. Its changes are removed."
fi
exit 0

nodes.label: Continue or halt
nodes.prompt: The night goes on only on a sound base. The orchestrator's report says whether this Feature is one; no report halts the night too.

options.name: halt
options.description: Work on top of this code would be wrong, or the orchestrator gave no verdict. The night stops for the owner.

options.name: continue
options.description: The work is a sound base: the night goes on with the next Feature.
